newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TITLE BECKONS NEW ERA FOR 'RAUL' MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TITLE BECKONS NEW ERA FOR 'RAUL' MADRID.

text.p: Six-times European champions Real Madrid return to the top continental competition minus the mastermind behind their 27th league triumph but blessed with a new teenage hero.
Saturday's emphatic 3-1 victory over neighbours Atletico did not just close one of the bitterest chapters in the club's history, it also confirmed the emergence of Raul Gonzalez.
Raul was the centre of attention for the 800,000 fans who took to the streets of the Spanish capital to celebrate.
Following the victory, coach Fabio Capello revealed he was leaving the club after just a year in charge, ending a feud with president Fernando Sanz.
But the season will be remembered for the blossoming talent of Raul.

The title-clinching victory was a satisfying moment for the 19-year-old, who at times has had to struggle to escape the shadow of Alfonso Perez, the international striker who has now moved to Real Betis.
Some supporters found it difficult to forgive Raul his Atletico past, but on Saturday the fans adopted him as their own.
"The league crowns Raul," read a headline in the El Pais daily on Monday.
Raul, alongside teammate Fernando Hierro, was voted the best Spanish player in the league in a poll of managers organised by the paper.
Atletico let Raul go when the club decided to scrap junior sides in a cost-cutting measure.
Ironically, Raul seems to save his best performances for games against his former teammates, scoring Saturday's opening goal.
Raul was also in superb touch against Atletico earlier in the season, carrying his side to a memorable 4-1 victory.
And the teenager's first league goal -- scored from a superb pass by Danish master Michael Laudrup -- came against Atletico as a 17-year-old.

The then Real coach Jorge Valdano, who had plucked Raul from the club's third team, had risked the wrath of fans by picking Raul. The previous week he missed several simple chances in his league debut at Zaragoza.
"I've demonstrated that I'm not a whim of Valdano," said Raul after Saturday's match.
The Italian press were also seduced by the astonishing maturity of Spain's new media darling, baptising the team 'Raul' Madrid after his Champions' League performances last season.
Real enter next season's European Cup without Capello after his tumultuous season in charge.
Capello, who has said he is returning to AC Milan, will again miss out on the premier continental competition despite winning two of Europe's toughest leagues in successive seasons.
The Italian was head-hunted by Real after their disastrous season in 1995/6, which had seen the club fail to qualify for Europe for only the second time in their illustrious history.
But Saturday's victory and Capello's subsequent announcement that he was leaving Spain ended the uneasy truce between himself and Sanz.
"For me he's no longer Real coach," said Sanz.
"If Capello hasn't had my affection, then Real hasn't had his."
Within the next few days Sanz hopes to announce an agreement with Jupp Heynckes, the German manager who took unfancied Tenerife to this season's UEFA Cup semifinal.
"Heynckes will do it just as well (as Capello)," said Sanz. "The team, conveniently reinforced, will start amongst the favourites for the seventh (European) Cup."

Real, who already have Zaragoza striker Fernando Morientes lined up for next season, are thought to be renewing their efforts to secure the services of French internationals Christian Karembeu of Sampdoria and Monaco's Thierry Henry.
